neighbours.label: ' while' (also 'though'/'although') opening a parenthetical concessive clause right after a comma following a subject noun, e.g. 'The Republic, while asserting...'
fire: The Republic of Vietnam, while asserting its independence, still depended heavily on foreign aid for survival.
The disappearance of these grand printed volumes, while inevitable, is another sad sign of changing habits.
South Korea, while smaller than Japan, is already deeply engaged in regional trade negotiations.
The heavier ladder, while it costs more to build, will last for decades of regular use.
The President's power in foreign affairs, though questioned, has been constrained very little in recent years.
Her older brother, although quiet in public, was famously loud at home with his friends.
The guides, while sighted in the outer world, were helpless in the dark tunnels below.
The old bridge, while narrow, carried traffic across the river for nearly a century.
